target_customer: Crypto users who buy, sell and mint NFTs and other digital assets, and creators and projects listing them
problem: There was no open place to trade any NFT on Ethereum; early marketplaces were tied to single games such as CryptoKitties.
business_model: Marketplace take rate on secondary sales (a 2.5 percent fee is cited by one analysis)

founders.name: Devin Finzer
founders.background_notes: Per the YC company page: software engineer at Google and Pinterest, sold a previous company to Credit Karma.

founders.name: Alex Atallah
founders.background_notes: Named co-founder by Wikipedia, which says he left the company in July 2022. Background not found in opened sources.

competitors.name: Rare Bits
competitors.what: Marketplace for crypto collectibles and digital assets such as CryptoKitties
competitors.traction_then: Launched in February 2018 per Yahoo Finance coverage; user numbers not found

competitors.name: CryptoKitties own marketplace
competitors.what: Game with built-in trading of kitties charging a commission on sales
competitors.traction_then: Reported by one analysis at about 10 million dollars in sales within months of its November 2017 launch

technical_complexity.rationale: Indexing on-chain assets and building order books on Ethereum in 2017 and 2018 was new, but a small team could build it with standard web engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Liquidity and listings concentrated on OpenSea once collections listed there, but code was copyable and rivals such as Rarible and SuperRare appeared later.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Early rivals did not stop OpenSea; it became the dominant NFT venue in 2021.

market_need_then: CryptoKitties in late 2017 showed demand for NFTs but trading was confined to one game; the founders saw a gap for an open marketplace for any token and a lower fee than CryptoKitties per one analysis.

identity.logo: Sailboat in a circle, simplified in 2021 to a white ship in a blue circle with wordmark
identity.voice_and_tone: Open, builder oriented; calls itself an open digital economy

branding.community_and_virality: Became the default NFT venue during the 2021 boom, with extensive press coverage of the brand and its layoffs.

brand_strength.rationale: Became the best known NFT marketplace name in 2021 and 2022 per wide press coverage, though no source tied growth to the brand itself.

outcome_analysis: OpenSea launched as an open NFT marketplace in December 2017 and rode the 2021 NFT boom to a 1.5 billion dollar valuation in July 2021 and 13.3 billion in January 2022. When trading collapsed it cut about 20 percent of staff in July 2022 and about half in November 2023, and faced a regulatory notice. It remains operating with a smaller team and broader onchain focus.
notes: Layoff figures (20 percent July 2022, 50 percent November 2023) come from search result summaries of Axios and Decrypt, not opened pages. Atallah's prior employers were quoted in a search snippet but not read from an opened source, so left null. Series A date and amount come from Wikipedia and a search summary of other outlets. Total raised not stated in opened articles.
